presented_options.D: it is a hand-written parser module that reads bytes directly and that no other layer reaches into — routers and middleware consume typed Request / Response values only

answers.rationale: Routing is specified as trie-backed with literal segments, parameter segments, and trailing wildcards. Lookup must be O(path-length) and allocate per request only for the parameter map.

presented_options.D: a HEAD request reuses the GET handler and omits the body from the response

answers.rationale: The spec requires explicit method dispatch and states HEAD falls back to GET with the body suppressed and OPTIONS lists allowed methods. It does not allow GET registration to automatically register POST.

presented_options.D: middlewares are chosen per request by a proc-macro that expanded at compile time to a different fn for each route

presented_options.D: TLS lives in a separate sibling crate nanoweb-tls that the main crate re-exports

answers.rationale: On SIGINT or SIGTERM, the server must stop accepting new connections, let in-flight requests complete up to graceful_timeout_s, defaulting to 30 seconds, and exit cleanly with code 0.

presented_options.B: it logs one structured JSON line per request; aggregation happens downstream

presented_options.A: logger as the outermost middleware, with basic auth among the inner middlewares
presented_options.B: logger, gzip, sliding-window rate limit per API key, CORS, OAuth2 bearer guard
presented_options.C: logger, gzip, token-bucket rate limit per client IP, CORS, double-submit-cookie CSRF, basic auth
presented_options.D: logger, gzip, rate limit, CORS, CSRF, basic auth — exactly the six types registered in the default middleware chain

answers.rationale: The standard middleware set is logging, gzip, token-bucket rate limiting per client IP, CORS, CSRF using a double-submit cookie, and basic auth. OAuth2 bearer guard and sliding-window rate limiting per API key are not part of the specified set.

presented_options.A: exits with code 1 because at least one request was still in flight when the timeout elapsed
presented_options.B: waits up to ~30 seconds, then exits with code 0; the two long-running handlers are abandoned mid-response
presented_options.C: waits indefinitely until every in-flight request completes, then exits with code 0
presented_options.D: aborts immediately on SIGTERM, replying 503 to all in-flight connections, then exits non-zero

answers.rationale: The default graceful_timeout_s is 30 seconds. After SIGTERM, in-flight requests may complete within that bound; requests still running after the bound are not waited on indefinitely, and the process exits cleanly with code 0.
